candidate.title: hyRAD
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina 'Hybridization RAD (hyRAD) for degraded DNA' schematic, clarified by Suchan et al.'s hyRAD implementation: high-quality genomic DNA supplies size-selected ddRAD-derived DNA probes; a separate specimen-DNA shotgun library undergoes probe hybridization and streptavidin capture to yield enriched DNA. The card and verified collection-page heading/caption identify one target, hyRAD (hybridization RAD / Hybridization Capture Using RAD Probes). RAD-seq/ddRAD is the embedded probe-production component. The depicted capture substrate is a shotgun library; the catalogue's mention of capturing ddRAD libraries does not add an illustrated alternative. The far-left 'Genome' icon is a category illustration with no transfer arrow to the workflow. The schematic ends at DNA; downstream sequencing and SNP readout are interpreted from the paper without adding unshown operations.

states.label: DNA (enriched target shotgun library)
features: The final icon is labeled DNA and shows plain blue lines after streptavidin pull-down.

Primary-supported identity: target-specimen shotgun-library DNA recovered from probe complexes; library adaptors support subsequent amplification and sequencing despite their omission from the simplified endpoint icon.
The capture block transiently attaches probe–library complexes to beads; the terminal product is library DNA recovered from the probes.
Enriched for DNA homologous to the ddRAD-derived probes; captured fragments can extend beyond or incompletely overlap the original RAD locus and need not retain its flanking restriction sites.
Capture is an enrichment with possible background carryover, rather than a guarantee of pure target sequence or complete locus recovery.

Downstream sequencing reads specimen genomic sequence at recovered loci and supports SNP discovery/genotyping; the probes determine selection, while the target library is the intended sequenced carrier.

operations.label: Prepare RAD-seq library and size select
operations.description: Convert the high-quality genomic DNA into an adaptor-bearing, size-selected restriction-fragment library. The primary hyRAD implementation identifies this depicted RAD component as ddRAD; its output is the precursor used to make probes.
operations.mechanism: Double restriction digestion generates the genomic fragments; adaptor-bearing fragments undergo size selection. The broad library-preparation block is retained at the level depicted.
operations.information_effect: Restriction-fragment boundaries and size selection determine the genomic subset available for probe production. The material still carries probe-donor genomic sequence.

operations.label: Adaptor removal and labeling
operations.description: Remove adaptor sequences from the size-selected RAD library and biotin-label the remaining genomic fragments, converting library precursors into capture probes. Orange terminal segments disappear and blue stars appear in the drawn output.

operations.label: Hybridize to probes
operations.description: Bring the target shotgun library together with the biotinylated probes. Complementary library sequences pair with probes to produce the depicted probe–library complexes.
operations.mechanism: Sequence-complementary DNA hybridization associates probe-defined loci with target-library fragments.
operations.information_effect: Introduces a physical link between specimen-sequence carriers and biotinylated locus-selecting probes. Target-library fragments can overlap only part of a RAD locus or extend beyond it; capture does not require the original RAD flanking restriction sites in the target fragments.

operations.label: Streptavidin pull down
operations.description: Use streptavidin-covered beads to retain the biotinylated probes together with hybridized target-library DNA. The bead-associated intermediate is depicted within this capture block; its outgoing DNA product is interpreted from the primary paper as the enriched target library recovered from the probes.
operations.mechanism: The biotin–streptavidin attachment supplies the pull-down interface. Probe association retains target DNA during bead separation, followed by recovery of the target-library DNA as reported in the paper.
operations.information_effect: Changes the representation of the specimen shotgun library by enriching fragments associated with the probes. Sequencing the recovered library can establish genomic sequence and SNP variation at recovered loci, with background carryover and incomplete coverage limiting specificity and completeness.

method_scopes.rationale: All five depicted operations apply to the single hyRAD implementation illustrated here. The independent high-quality-DNA probe route and specimen-DNA shotgun route meet at hybridization, followed by streptavidin capture. The primary paper explicitly links these components and identifies the donor RAD component as ddRAD. The collection page is a verified secondary match because its heading and schematic caption both identify hyRAD. The unconnected far-left Genome category icon is descriptive; it does not establish another transformation or target method.

corrections.diagram_observation: The outgoing product after the bead is labeled 'DNA' and drawn as two plain blue lines. Orange adaptor segments and star-marked probes are not displayed at this endpoint; no adaptor-removal step is drawn on the target-library route.
corrections.primary_statement: Suchan et al. report that the hybridization-enriched product is recovered from the probes, then describe the captured material as libraries amplified using P1/P2 library primers and sequenced as enriched shotgun libraries. Accordingly s_enriched is authored as recovered target-library DNA retaining the library interface; the simple final icon is not evidence that capture removes target adaptors or that probe DNA is the intended sequenced product.
